chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

We came to the door of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام while we were seeking permission to enter upon him. We heard him speaking words that were not Arabic, so we supposed that they were in Syriac. Then he wept, and we wept because of his weeping. Then the servant came out to us and gave us permission, so we entered upon him.

So I said: 'May Allah keep you well, we came to you seeking permission to enter upon you, and we heard you speaking words that were not Arabic, so we supposed that they were in Syriac. Then you wept, so we wept because of your weeping.' He عليه السلام said: 'Yes. I remembered Ilyas the Prophet, and he was among the devoted worshippers from the prophets of the Children of Israel.'

So I said: 'Like what he used to say in his sajdah?' Then he spoke it in Syriac, and by Allah, we had not seen any priest or catholicos more eloquent in pronunciation than he was in it. Then he explained it to us in Arabic and said: 'He used to say in his sajdah: Will You punish me while I have made my hot middays thirsty for You? Will You punish me while I have rubbed my face in the dust for You? Will You punish me while I have avoided acts of disobedience for You? Will You punish me while I have kept my night awake for You?'

He عليه السلام said: 'Then Allah revealed to him: Raise your head, for I shall not punish you. He said: Then he said: If You say, "I will not punish you," then were You to punish me, what would that be? Am I not Your servant and You my Lord? He عليه السلام said: Then Allah revealed to him: Raise your head, for I shall not punish you. Indeed, when I promise a promise, I fulfill it.'

key_terms.أَوْحَى اللَّهُ: Allah revealed; indicating divine communication to the prophet
key_terms.إِلْيَاسَ النَّبِيَّ: Ilyas the Prophet; the prophet whose supplication is being recalled
key_terms.الْمَعَاصِيَ: acts of disobedience; sins that the supplicant says he avoided for Allah
key_terms.بِالسُّرْيَانِيَّةِ: in Syriac; the language in which the Imam عليه السلام was heard speaking
key_terms.سُجُودِهِ: his sajdah; the state of prostration in which the supplication was said
key_terms.مُعَذِّبِي: punishing me; central term repeated in the supplication
key_terms.وَعْدًا: a promise; referring to Allah’s promise not to punish him
key_terms.وَفَيْتُ بِهِ: I fulfill it; affirming that Allah fulfills His promise

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show that the Imam عليه السلام knew the languages of earlier revelation and the supplication of Ilyas عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام spoke in Syriac while recalling the supplication of Ilyas عليه السلام in sajdah, demonstrating knowledge of revealed languages. It preserves a devotional supplication centered on humility, worship, and hope in Allah’s fulfilled promise. The report also reflects the Imams’ connection to the legacy of earlier prophets and scriptures.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

‘We came over to the door of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and we wanted the permission to (see) him<sup>asws</sup>. So we heard him<sup>asws</sup> speak in a speech which wasn’t Arabic. So we were under the impression that it was Assyrian. Then he<sup>asws</sup> cried. So we cried upon his<sup>asws</sup> crying. Then the boy came out to us, and permitted for us. So we entered to (see) him<sup>asws</sup>.

So I said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! We came over to you<sup>asws</sup> wanting the permission to (see) you<sup>asws</sup>, and we heard you<sup>asws</sup> speaking with a speech which wasn’t Arabic. So we were under the impression that it is Assyrian. Then you cried, so we cried upon your<sup>asws</sup> crying’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. I<sup>asws</sup> remembered Ilyas<sup>as</sup> the Prophet<sup>as</sup>, and he<sup>as</sup> was from the most devoted of the worshippers of the Children of Israel’.

So I said, ‘Just as he<sup>as</sup> was saying in his<sup>as</sup> Sajdah?’. Then he spoke regarding it in Assyrian, so by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, we had neither seen a Pastor nor a Vicar more eloquent in tone than he<sup>asws</sup> was with it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> interpreted it for us in Arabic, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>as</sup> was saying in his<sup>as</sup> Sajdah: ‘Will You<sup>azwj</sup> Punish me<sup>as</sup> and I<sup>as</sup> have kept my<sup>as</sup> mouth thirsty for You<sup>azwj</sup>? Will You<sup>azwj</sup> Punish me<sup>as</sup> and I<sup>as</sup> have rubbed my<sup>as</sup> face in the dust for You<sup>azwj</sup>? Will You<sup>azwj</sup> Punish me<sup>as</sup> and I<sup>as</sup> have kept aside from my<sup>as</sup> disobediences for You<sup>azwj</sup>? Will You<sup>azwj</sup> Punish me<sup>as</sup> and I<sup>as</sup> have held vigils for You<sup>azwj</sup> during my<sup>as</sup> nights?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “Raise your<sup>as</sup> head, for I<sup>azwj</sup> will not Punish you<sup>as</sup>”. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘If You<sup>azwj</sup> Say: “I<sup>azwj</sup> will not Punish you<sup>as</sup>”, then if You<sup>azwj</sup> do Punish me<sup>as</sup>, what would that be? Am I<sup>as</sup> not Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant and You<sup>azwj</sup> my<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “Raise your<sup>as</sup> head, for I<sup>azwj</sup> will not Punish you<sup>as</sup>! I<sup>azwj</sup>, when I<sup>azwj</sup> Promise a Promise, I<sup>azwj</sup> Fulfil it!’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Bakr ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following.

“We went to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and wanted permission. We heard him speaking in a none Arabic language and we thought it was Suryani (0r Syrian) language. The Imams (a.s.) then wept and we did so because of his weeping. A boy then came out to give us permission for a meeting.

In the meeting I asked him, “May Allah keep you well, we came to ask permission for a meeting and we heard you speak in a none Arabic language and we thought it was Suryani language. Then we heard you weeping and because of that we also wept.” The Imams (a.s.) said, “Yes, I remembered prophet Ilyas, one of the Israelite prophets and devoted in worship.

I then said what he used to say in his prostration. He then went into it in Suryani language. Swearing to Allah, we had not seen any monk or minister as eloquent in it as he in it. He then explained it to us in Arabic, “Ilyas would say in his prostration, ‘O Lord, will I find you punish me although you know of thirst in the heat of the midday? Will I find you punish me although you know that I rub my face on earth to worship you? Will I find you punish me although you know that I give up sins for you? Will I find you punish me although you know that I stay awake all night just for you?”

The Imams (a.s.) then said, “Allah then told him through inspiration, “Rise your head from the earth. I will not punish you.” The Imams (a.s.) then said that he said to Allah, “What if say, “I will not punish you but then you punished me? Am I not your slave and you are my Lord.” The Imams (a.s.) said, “Allah then spoke to him through inspiration, “Rise your head. I will not punish you because when I promise I then keep My promise.”
